data.text:
# Blender Showcase: Jelly Dance
A skinned, animated glTF model (Model node) danced on the beat by a Render 3D node: 7 instances in a ring, soft shadows, a spot light from the surface, caustics on the sand, fog and bloom.
- The model is self-made (scripts/make-test-glb.mjs, CC0): a body + 6 tentacles skinned to 37 bones, clips "Sway" and "Dance".
- Clip time = Beat.time / 2: the Dance clip (1 s, two bounces) lands every bounce on a beat.

## Your own Blender model
- Blender: File > Export > glTF 2.0 (.glb). Mesh: UVs, normals, vertex colours, apply modifiers. Animation: actions / NLA strips become clips; armature deform bones only. Leave Compression (Draco) off.
- Drop the .glb on the canvas (or double-click the Model node, or MCP load_model). Up to 15 MB it is saved inside the project.
- Pick the clip with the Clip param (index), wire any time into Model.time.

## Scene
Sand floor (PBR + caustics on Surface.position), deep-sea backdrop per camera ray, fog matched to the water colour, directional light with shadows plus a spot from the surface that pulses on the beat.

## Music
drive = music x smoothstep(0.02, 0.12, level) swings the ring faster; beat pulses flare the spot light and the bloom: Beat (clock stable, gate fade) pulse x confidence, so they come from the stable beat clock and fade out while it is unsure (a track change) and with the audio off. The model's animation runs on Beat.time of the same stable clock: it never jumps, it glides to a new tempo.
